public_sources.title: Uesato et al., Rigorous Agent Evaluation: An Adversarial Approach to Uncover Catastrophic Failures
observed_results: The method learns an adversarial value/failure predictor by continuation from weaker or noisier agents, then uses it to choose evaluation initial conditions and importance-correct failure-probability estimates.

Failure search median sample acceleration versus random testing is 198x in simulated Driving and 3100x in Humanoid. Median expected wall-clock failure search is 2.7 hours random versus 1.1 minutes AVF on Driving; including 5 minutes AVF training gives 27x total speedup. Humanoid is 77 hours random versus 6 minutes AVF search; including 70 minutes AVF training gives 61x total speedup.
At 95% confidence for a 3-approximation of failure probability, AVF uses 750 vs 11,000 experiments on Driving (14x fewer) and 15,000 vs 510,000 on Humanoid (34x fewer).

A simpler prioritized-replay baseline can fail to discover existing failures; the paper explicitly falls back to vanilla Monte Carlo after exhausting known training failures. The authors also argue binary rare failures make direct cross-entropy/subset methods hard on the final robust agent and use continuation from weaker agents to create learning signal.

public_sources.title: Liu et al., Adaptive Multilevel Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo for Rare Events Estimation in Language Models
observed_ablation_results: At toxic-story gamma*=7 with p_MC=3.81e-6, samples per adaptation level have a strong non-linear effect: 256 gives 93.1% error, 512 gives 36.4%, 1024 gives 28.3%, 1536 gives 22.3%, and 2048 gives 12.8%, while runtime increases from 2.35 to 8.82 minutes.

The retained-level fraction rho is also non-monotone in finite samples: rho=0.30 gives 28.3% error, 0.45 gives 43.0%, 0.52 gives 70.3%, 0.58 gives 37.0%, and 0.65 gives 42.3%. Higher rho does not automatically improve estimation despite changing hit rate/ESS.

The appendix explicitly notes that on a less-rare threshold gamma*=4, the proposed method can have higher relative error than both baselines despite higher hit rate and ESS. Hit rate/ESS therefore cannot be treated as direct probability-accuracy metrics.
Under an imperfect score, proposal learning cannot remove score-induced bias; the paper separates score mismatch from proposal-dependent sampling error.

derived_results.claim: For rare agent failures with weak binary signal, a continuation curriculum over related weaker/noisier policies is a quantitatively strong alternative to learning the rare-event proposal only on the final robust agent. Historical training trajectories become labeled continuation data for a failure predictor; importance sampling then focuses evaluation on high predicted failure regions while retaining probability correction. External evidence shows 198x/3100x median failure-search episode reduction and 14x/34x fewer experiments for risk estimation in Driving/Humanoid.

The combined Uesato/Liu evidence supports an explicit three-object interface for rare evaluation: (1) score or failure predictor used to rank/select scenarios, (2) proposal/adversary used to concentrate samples, and (3) importance-corrected estimator used for probability. Search success, hit rate, ESS and prediction quality are diagnostics for objects 1/2, not substitutes for object 3.

Multilevel rarity controls should be treated as a tunable budget controller rather than a fixed 'more intermediate levels is safer' heuristic. The recent LLM ablation shows both samples-per-level and retained fraction rho have finite-budget failure regimes. Therefore a robust adaptation should optimize rho/level count jointly with per-level sample allocation under held-out probability error or a certified variance target, not hit rate alone.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Uesato et al. evaluate simulated Driving and Humanoid, not modern LLM agents. Their failure predictor uses initial-condition distributions and historical weaker-agent data; direct transfer to tool-using multi-turn LLM agents remains an untested hypothesis.
The AVF proposal can under-sample unknown failure regions; the paper notes coverage is essential because importance weights can otherwise explode. Prioritized replay alone may miss failures entirely.

Continuation assumes weaker/noisier agents reveal failure geometry relevant to the final agent. If capability improvements qualitatively create new failure modes, historical continuation data can be misleading.
The 2026 LLM rho ablation contradicts any simple monotonic rule that larger retained fraction or larger hit rate guarantees lower probability-estimation error.
No local AGI/system claim follows from the external agent-evaluation speedups.

candidate_update.rare_event_agent_evaluation: new strong candidate: continuation-trained adversarial failure predictor + importance-corrected risk estimator, with explicit coverage fallback
candidate_update.adaptive_multilevel_llm: failure envelope strengthened: sample budget and rho must be optimized against estimator accuracy/variance, not hit rate or ESS alone

frontier: Search for post-2024 rare-event evaluation of tool-using or multi-turn LLM agents with trajectory-level failures and unbiased/importance-corrected risk estimates. Prefer methods with replayable simulator state and explicit coverage diagnostics.

Investigate whether SCARCE (2026) or related learned-embedding subset simulation yields a probability-valid trajectory-evaluation mechanism rather than only failure discovery; extract exact guarantee and matched baselines before promotion.

Develop a testable adaptation schema: continuation source set, coverage floor/fallback to base sampling, proposal ESS/weight-tail alarm, and held-out probability-error evaluation. Keep failure search and risk estimation as separate endpoints.
For the recent multilevel LLM method, derive a budget-aware policy over rho and samples per level from the reported ablation; do not overfit a single rho=0.3 setting.
exact_next_action: Investigate 2026 learned-embedding/subset-simulation rare-event work and recent multi-turn LLM/agent safety evaluation. Require a probability-valid estimator, not just adversarial discovery. Compare its coverage mechanism to AVF importance sampling and progressive twisted SMC. In parallel formalize a fallback condition: if proposal ESS/importance-weight tail or held-out coverage degrades, route a fixed fraction of budget back to base-distribution sampling.
